findings.where: The 'Get Mark's briefings on PPP reform' band directly under the hero, at both widths
findings.fault: The house blue changes job here. The page's own palette gives it the first-screen action, the wordmark, links and the curve. In this band it becomes a full-bleed section ground, the largest blue area on the page. Its hard edge sits right against the slate hero, at 2.47:1 with no warm-white gap between them, so blue no longer reads as 'the action'. The page now has three strong grounds (slate, blue, then warm white) where the brief asked for one ground, one ink and at most one accent, with v7's page below set in grey on warm white.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for blue as the one accent and the page below in grey on warm white. A visitor scrolling from the hero meets a second, larger blue field that outweighs the blue 'Write to me directly' box. The one personal contact loses its claim to being the page's blue.

findings.where: The article specimen's PDF card ('Streamlining the PPP Process…', Lecture · 23 April 2026)
findings.fault: This one card has its own surface language: a pale blue tint fill, a blue hairline border, a wide soft drop shadow and rounded corners. Everything else on the page is flat and square-cornered: the action box, the Subscribe button, the photographs and the palette swatches. The fill tint appears nowhere in the palette. A hairline border with a wide soft shadow on one resting element breaks the house surface rule, and a strong border on top of a fill step doubles the edge.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Angélique. The PDF list is meant to be the product below the fold, and it arrives looking like a pasted-in UI widget from another system. Every future PDF entry would carry this off-palette, off-system styling.

findings.where: The hero lockup (aqueduct mark and 'MMM INFRA' wordmark at top left, reversed to warm white), and the same lockup in the motion-sketch thumbnail
findings.fault: The logo appears in a reversed warm-white version that the client does not hold. The only copy on file is the full-colour JPEG, and the brand sheet records no white version. The footer shows the real full-colour lockup (grey mark, blue wordmark), so the page presents two colourings of the same logo.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo colours are fixed until he opens them. A reversed version may be made only with his yes, and none is recorded. The founder would have to answer for an unapproved logo version on the first screen he judges.

findings.where: Blue on static parts: the 'PALETTE' label, and the numbers of the article's three-item list
findings.fault: The page states 'Grey for reading, blue only where something can be clicked', and its palette table lists blue for links. Yet the static section label and the list numbers are in the link blue, and the parts map confirms that neither does anything.
findings.who_objects: A reader of an article page who has learnt that blue means a link will pause on blue numerals that do nothing. Angélique's later pages would inherit the mixed rule.
